## Claude — 2026-10-05 07:19

I've gone through everything: the VO, the 12 app screens, the 49-page brand book, the colour sheet and the existing MP4. Below is the plan, then some questions for you before I start building.

## What I found in your materials
- **Voiceover:** 3:14.8, English (ElevenLabs "Adam"). The video will be cut to match it exactly.
- **App screens (12):** onboarding, login, map with towers, 3D city view, listings, price filter, mortgage calculator, splash, profile/customer portal, deposit payment, gallery, and the Arqan Waterfront project page. They are WhatsApp-compressed, 736×1600.
- **Brand book:** colours are Navy #041E42, Beige #DBC8B6, Rose Gold #A27063 and Sky #9BCBEB. Headlines use Canela, body text uses Vazirmatn. The visual idea is "Everyday Flow": the S-curve from the logo turns into lines, patterns and transitions. Materials are copper, wood and frosted glass.
- **MP4 (3:00, 1024×576):** a line-art animatic in navy and gold with Arabic captions. It covers the same story: paperwork, then the phone, then the four journeys, construction progress, community, the yield manager, and the ZOOD end card.

## Creative direction
Apple-style keynote film. Mostly deep navy, with warm beige "daylight" sections, rose-gold accents and a slow camera.
- **Recurring motif:** a thin rose-gold S-curve from the logo draws itself on screen. It links every scene and also works as the transition.
- **Phones:** realistic iPhone 17 Pro-style mockups with a titanium frame, Dynamic Island, glass reflections and soft shadows. They float and turn in 3D, and the app screens scroll and get tapped inside them.
- **Text:** large serif headlines with blur-in, word-by-word reveals timed to the VO.
- **Spelling:** "ZOOD" is in capitals everywhere.

## Storyboard (times are approximate; I'll sync to the VO exactly)
| # | Time | VO | Visuals |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0:00–0:25 | "Luxury… More presence. More living…" | Black fades to navy and the gold curve draws itself. Each "More…" word appears on its own beat over slow push-ins on interiors and towers. |
| 2 | 0:25–0:40 | "…not a promise on paper. It is an experience you live." | Serif statement scene. A beige light sweep, copper texture. |
| 3 | 0:40–0:52 | "Traditionally… paperwork, spreadsheets…" | Line-art documents, spreadsheets and chat bubbles pile up messily, then get pulled into one point of light. |
| 4 | 0:52–1:10 | "We build communities… Four journeys… One application. This is the ZOOD app." | That light becomes the phone, which opens on the splash screen ("Live in Luxury, Live in ZOOD"). Four words (Discover / Create / Live / Enjoy) merge into one app icon. Hero shot of the phone rotating. |
| 5 | 1:10–1:40 | Discover: "Explore every destination… compare side by side… filter" | Onboarding, then the map pins (Tower A–D), the 3D city view, two phones comparing listings side by side, and the price-range filter animating live. |
| 6 | 1:40–2:00 | Own: "Verify identity… book a visit… sign digitally" | Login, an identity check ring, a reserve button, a contract with a swipe-to-sign signature, then the deposit payment screen. |
| 7 | 2:00–2:20 | "Every payment… track construction… handover" | Profile payments bar (7 of 12 paid), a progress ring counting 36%→40%, a milestone timeline, the Arqan Waterfront page, and a key/handover moment. |
| 8 | 2:20–2:40 | Live: "your community… day and night" | Customer portal, noticeboard and service chips (Cleaning, Delivery, Facilities), the gallery, and a light shift from day to night. |
| 9 | 2:40–2:58 | Invest: "Long-term leasing. Short stays. Or selling." | A Yield Manager toggle that snaps on each word as it's spoken, plus the mortgage calculator figures counting up. |
| 10 | 2:58–3:15 | "Discover… Live luxury. Live ZOOD." | **Apple-style finale:** every screen flies in as a rounded tile and settles into a bento grid around the centre phone. The grid then folds inward into the ZOOD logo, the curve draws under it, and the end card reads "Live luxury. Live ZOOD." |

Some of the features in the VO have no screen yet: 3D unit walkthrough, compare, ID verification, e-signing, construction tracking, community and yield manager. I'll design these as brand-consistent UI in the same style as your screens, using the animatic's ideas as the starting point.

## Production
- **Tools:** Remotion (React to MP4), rendered here. The source project goes on branch `claude/intelligent-allen-jrzv18`, so your team can edit text and timing later.
- **Review steps:** first a storyboard of still frames for each scene, then a low-res draft, then the final render.
- **Default output:** 1920×1080, 30fps, H.264, with your VO mixed in.

## Questions
1. **Logo:** do you have a vector file (SVG/AI/EPS) for the symbol and lockups? Otherwise I'll redraw it from the brand book, which will be less exact.
2. **Fonts:** do you have the Canela font files (it needs a commercial licence)? If not, I'll use a close free serif.
3. **Screens:** can you send the originals exported from Figma at @3x PNG? The WhatsApp copies will look soft in close-ups. Is it OK for me to design the missing feature screens listed above?
4. **The MP4:** is it a reference for style and timing, or footage you want to see in the film? Right now I plan to treat it as reference only.
5. **Language:** should on-screen text be English only, or English and Arabic?
6. **Wording of the four journeys:** the VO ending says "Discover. Enjoy. Live. Dwell." but the animatic shows Discover / Own / Live / Invest (اكتشف · امتلك · عِش · استثمر). Which words should go on screen?
7. **Music:** do you have a licensed background track? If not, I'll deliver a VO-only mix, timed so a track is easy to add later.
8. **Project imagery:** do you have real ZOOD renders or drone footage? Otherwise I'll use the images from the screens and the brand book.
9. **Output and end card:** do you need 4K or 60fps? Should the end card include App Store / Google Play badges, a launch date or zood.sa?

Answer whatever you can. For anything you skip, I'll use the defaults above and start with the storyboard frames.

Thanks, I've checked everything you sent. Here's the updated plan. I won't start building until you approve it.

## What changed with your new files
- **Logo:** the SVG has a 4096×2304 transparent PNG inside it, so it's sharp enough for full-screen use. I'll also make white and rose-gold versions of it for the dark scenes.
- **Font:** ITF Huwiya includes full English letters and numbers. I'll use it for all on-screen text: Light and Regular weights, widely spaced, for headlines, and Medium for labels.
- **New screens:** Community, Yield Manager, 3D Walkthrough, Compare, E-Signing and Construction Tracking. They're clean, high-res, and fill almost every gap. Identity verification still has no screen, so I'll animate a Face ID-style scan over your Login screen.
- **On-screen text:** English only. "ZOOD" is always in capitals. The four journeys are written as **Discover / Own / Live / Invest**, even though the VO near the end says "Discover. Enjoy. Live. Dwell."
- **Images:** taken only from the app screens and the brand book.

## ⚠️ Music: I need your help with one thing
This cloud environment's network policy blocks music sites (pixabay.com, youtube.com and mixkit.co were all refused). I can't download a track until one of these happens:
- **(a) You upload the MP3 here.** I'd look for a "luxury cinematic corporate / ambient piano with soft pulse" track, about 3:30, that builds slowly and swells at the end.
- **(b) You allow `pixabay.com` and `cdn.pixabay.com`.** Go to the environment menu in the session title bar → Edit → Network access → Custom (keep the package-manager defaults). Then I'll choose and download the track myself.

Please don't use a track ripped from YouTube. Most are copyrighted, and a commercial client video can get claimed or taken down. Pixabay, Artlist or Epidemic tracks are safe to use. Meanwhile I'll build everything with the VO and add the music when we have it.

## Storyboard (timed to the actual pauses in the VO)
| # | Time | VO | Visuals |

| 5 | 1:12–1:26 | "Four journeys. Not four applications. One application. This is the ZOOD app." | Four cards (**Discover · Own · Live · Invest**) fly in and merge into a single phone. The ZOOD logo lands on it. |
| 6 | 1:26–1:57 | **Discover**: explore, rotate the model, walk through, real-time units, compare, filter | Onboarding → map with tower pins → 3D city view → **3D Walkthrough** (zoom into the floor plan) → listings → **Compare** (two phones side by side) → price-range filter. |
| 7 | 1:57–2:16 | **Own**: verify identity, book a visit, reserve, review and sign the contract | Login with a Face ID scan → deposit payment → **E-Signing**: the signature draws itself and the "Sign Document" button gets tapped. |

"Discover · Own · Live · Invest" appears, the grid folds into the ZOOD logo, the curve draws under "Live luxury. Live ZOOD.", and the end card shows the **App Store / Google Play** badges. |

**Tool · Bash** — Create Playwright contact sheet helper and run it

````
mkdir -p tools && cat > tools/sheet.mjs <<'EOF'
// Usage: node tools/sheet.mjs out.jpg cols thumbW thumbH file1 file2 ...
import { chromium } from 'playwright-core';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'url';
import path from 'path';
const [out, cols, w, h, ...files] = process.argv.slice(2);
const html = `<body style="margin:0;background:#111;display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(${cols},${w}px);gap:4px;font:12px sans-serif;color:#f55">` +
  files.map(f => `<div style="position:relative;width:${w}px;height:${h}px"><img src="${pathToFileURL(path.resolve(f))}" style="width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:contain"><span style="position:absolute;left:2px;top:2px;background:#000a">${path.basename(f)}</span></div>`).join('') + '</body>';
const b = await chromium.launch({ executablePath: '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome', args: ['--allow-file-access-from-files'] });
const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width: cols * (+w + 4), height: 100 } });
await p.setContent(html, { waitUntil: 'load' });
await p.goto('about:blank'); await p.setContent(html); await p.waitForLoadState('load');
await p.waitForTimeout(500);
await p.screenshot({ path: out, fullPage: true, type: 'jpeg', quality: 80 });
await b.close();
EOF

await p.goto('about:blank'); await p.setContent(html); await p.waitForLoadState('load');""","""const tmp = out + '.html'; (await import('fs')).writeFileSync(tmp, html);
await p.goto(pathToFileURL(path.resolve(tmp)).href, { waitUntil: 'load' });""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

// Shared helpers for the ZOOD film. Everything is driven by one paused GSAP
// timeline (`tl`) so any frame can be rendered deterministically via __seek(t).

const W = 1920, H = 1080;
const SCREEN_ASPECT = 0.46;            // width / height of the app screenshots
const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
const stage = document.getElementById('stage');
const A = (p) => `assets/${p}`;
const SCR = (n) => A(`screens/${n}`);
const PH = (n) => A(`photos/${n}`);

const EASE = 'power3.out', EASE_IO = 'power2.inOut', EASE_IN = 'power2.in';

function el(html, parent) {
  const t = document.createElement('template');
  t.innerHTML = html.trim();
  const e = t.content.firstElementChild;
  if (parent) parent.appendChild(e);
  return e;
}

function layer(cls = '', parent = stage) {
  const e = el(`<div class="layer ${cls}"></div>`, parent);
  gsap.set(e, { autoAlpha: 0 });
  return e;
}

// Fade a layer in at tIn and out at tOut.
function show(e, tIn, tOut, fin = 0.7, fout = 0.7) {
  tl.fromTo(e, { autoAlpha: 0 }, { autoAlpha: 1, duration: fin, ease: 'none', immediateRender: false }, tIn);
  if (tOut != null) tl.to(e, { autoAlpha: 0, duration: fout, ease: 'none' }, tOut);
}
function cut(e, tIn, tOut) {
  tl.set(e, { autoAlpha: 1 }, tIn);
  if (tOut != null) tl.set(e, { autoAlpha: 0 }, tOut);
}

// ---------- deterministic random ----------
function rng(seed) {
  return () => { seed |= 0; seed = seed + 0x6D2B79F5 | 0; let t = Math.imul(seed ^ seed >>> 15, 1 | seed);
    t = t + Math.imul(t ^ t >>> 7, 61 | t) ^ t; return ((t ^ t >>> 14) >>> 0) / 4294967296; };
}

// ---------- text ----------
// text: string; "|" forces a line break; words wrapped in [..] get the rose-gold treatment.
function text(str, cls, style = '', parent) {
  const lines = str.split('|').map(line => {
    const parts = line.trim().match(/\[[^\]]+\]|\S+/g) || [];
    return '<span class="line">' + parts.map((p, i) => {
      const rose = p.startsWith('[');
      const words = rose ? p.slice(1, -1).split(' ') : [p];
      return words.map((w, j) => `<span class="w${rose ? ' rose' : ''}">${w}${(j < words.length - 1 || i < parts.length - 1) ? ' ' : ''}</span>`).join('');
    }).join('') + '</span>';
  }).join('');
  return el(`<div class="abs ${cls}" style="${style}">${lines}</div>`, parent);
}

// Word-by-word blur reveal.
function reveal(e, t, { stagger = 0.07, dur = 1.0, y = 36, blur = 14 } = {}) {
  tl.set(e, { autoAlpha: 1 }, t);

// ZOOD app film — full timeline. Times are seconds into the voiceover
// (word timings from tools/vo-words.json, force-aligned to the VO).

// Full-width centred text.
const ctext = (s, cls, top, parent, extra = '') => text(s, cls, `left:0;width:${W}px;top:${top}px;text-align:center;${extra}`, parent);
const ltext = (s, cls, left, top, parent, extra = '') => text(s, cls, `left:${left}px;top:${top}px;${extra}`, parent);

function swapWords(list, parent, mk) {
  // list: [[str, t], ...]; each replaces the previous.
  const els = list.map(([s]) => mk(s));
  els.forEach((e, i) => {
    reveal(e, list[i][1], { stagger: 0.04, dur: 0.8 });
    if (i < list.length - 1) hide(e, list[i + 1][1] - 0.12, 0.35, -18);
  });
  return els;
}

function chapterTitle(word, t, { left = null, top = 440, parent, color = 'cream' } = {}) {
  const e = left == null ? ctext(word, `h0 ${color}`, top, parent, 'letter-spacing:.04em')
                         : ltext(word, `h0 ${color}`, left, top, parent, 'letter-spacing:.04em');
  reveal(e, t, { stagger: 0, dur: 0.7, blur: 24, y: 10 });
  tl.fromTo(e, { scale: 1.06 }, { scale: 1, duration: 1.2, ease: 'power2.out', immediateRender: false }, t);
  tl.to(e, { autoAlpha: 0, filter: 'blur(14px)', duration: 0.45, ease: EASE_IN }, t + 0.85);
}

const chapterLabels = [];
function chapterLabel(num, word, tIn, tOut, color = 'cream') {
  chapterLabels.push([num, word, tIn, tOut, color]);
}

function chip(html, x, y, parent, cls = '') {

}

import { chromium } from 'playwright-core';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'url';
import path from 'path';

export const ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname), '..');
const EXE = process.env.CHROME || '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1194/chrome-linux/headless_shell';

export async function openFilm() {
  const browser = await chromium.launch({
    executablePath: EXE,
    args: ['--allow-file-access-from-files', '--disable-web-security', '--hide-scrollbars', '--force-color-profile=srgb', '--font-render-hinting=none'],
  });
  const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1920, height: 1080 }, deviceScaleFactor: 1 });
  const errors = [];
  page.on('pageerror', (e) => errors.push(e.message));
  page.on('console', (m) => { if (m.type() === 'error' || m.type() === 'warning') errors.push(m.text()); });
  await page.goto(pathToFileURL(path.join(ROOT, 'src/index.html')).href, { waitUntil: 'load' });
  await page.waitForFunction(() => window.__ready !== undefined, null, { timeout: 30000 }).catch(() => {});
  await page.evaluate(() => window.__ready);
  if (errors.length) console.error('[page]', errors.join('\n'));
  const duration = await page.evaluate(() => window.DURATION);
  const cdp = await page.context().newCDPSession(page);
  async function frame(t, format = 'jpeg', quality = 95) {
    await page.evaluate((t) => window.__seek(t), t);
    const { data } = await cdp.send('Page.captureScreenshot', { format, quality: format === 'jpeg' ? quality : undefined, optimizeForSpeed: true });
    return Buffer.from(data, 'base64');
  }
  return { browser, page, frame, duration, errors };
}
EOF

**Tool · Bash** — Gitignore client assets, add README, stage files

````
printf "node_modules/\nout/\n# Client assets (licensed font, unreleased app screens, brand imagery, voiceover) are kept out of this public repo.\nsrc/assets/\n" > .gitignore && cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# ZOOD — App Launch Film

A 3:21 landscape (1920×1080, 60fps) launch film for the ZOOD mobile app, built as code:
an HTML/CSS stage animated by a single paused GSAP timeline, rendered frame-by-frame with
headless Chromium (Playwright) and encoded with ffmpeg.

## Structure
| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `src/index.html` | The 1920×1080 stage |
| `src/style.css` | Brand tokens (Navy #041E42, Beige #DBC8B6, Rose Gold #A27063, Sky #9BCBEB), type scale, phone mockup |
| `src/lib.js` | Helpers: text reveals, iPhone mockup, screen push, tap ripples, counters, brand curve lines |
| `src/scenes.js` | The whole timeline, scene by scene. Times are seconds into the VO |
| `src/boot.js` | Grain/vignette, asset preloading, `__seek(t)` API, `?play` live preview |
| `render/render.mjs` | Parallel frame renderer → MP4 with VO |
| `render/still.mjs` | Render stills at given times for review |
| `tools/vo-words.json` | Word-level timings of the voiceover (forced alignment) |

## Assets (not in git)
The repository is public, so client material is not committed. Place it in `src/assets/`:
`fonts/` (ITF Huwiya Arabic TTFs), `screens/` (app screens), `photos/` (brand-book imagery),
`brand/` (logo PNGs, App Store / Google Play SVGs), `audio/vo.mp3`.

## Usage
```bash
npm install
node render/still.mjs out/stills 10 65 120 198      # review frames
node render/render.mjs --fps 60 --workers 4 --out out/ZOOD_App_Film_1080p60.mp4
```
Open `src/index.html?play` in a browser and click to preview in real time with the VO.

## Editing
Copy and timings live in `src/scenes.js`. Each block is headed with its time range, and every
cue is keyed to a VO word time (see `tools/vo-words.json`).
EOF
git add -A && git status --short | head -20
````

I watched frames from every scene of the finished file and they look right. The animations are timed to the exact moments the narrator says each word.

**What's in it, in order:**
1. **Opening:** "Luxury." with the rose-gold curve from the logo drawing itself, then "More presence / living / personalization…" over photos from the brand book.
2. **"Experience you live":** a beige section with an arch-shaped photo reveal, ending on the ZOOD reception photo.
3. **The old way:** line drawings of paperwork, spreadsheets and messages pile up, then all get pulled into one point of light.
4. **One app:** four cards (Discover · Own · Live · Invest) shrink into app icons, merge into one ZOOD icon, and that turns into the phone.
5. **The four journeys**, using your screens in realistic iPhone mockups:
   - **Discover:** map, 3D city, and the floor plan pulled out of the phone and rotated in 3D, then compare and filter.

   - **Live:** home and property screens, community, services, and the background moving from day to night.
   - **Invest:** Yield Manager with a Long-term / Short stays / Sale toggle that switches as each option is spoken.
6. **Finale:** a wall of all 18 screens, then the grid of blocks. The blocks fold into the app icon, which becomes the ZOOD logo with "Live luxury. Live ZOOD." The end card shows the App Store and Google Play badges and zood.sa.

## Claude — 2026-10-05 11:28

I watched your MP4 again, every 2 seconds this time. It's the line-art animatic, and it has some strong ideas the current film doesn't use: the skyline drawing itself, the phone sketched in lines, the stacked floors ("Floor 12"), the unit-availability grid with a compare card, the isometric room with a Modern/Classic toggle, swipe-to-sign, the payment ring, snag pins on a floor plan, the title deed with a vault lock, and the services pie chart with a noticeboard.

Here's the plan for the remake.

## The approach: keep about half, rethink the other half
**Keeping:** the overall story order, the brand look (navy, beige, rose gold, Huwiya font), the realistic iPhone mockups with your real screens, the four chapters, and the Apple-style blocks finale with the end card.

**Changing:** pacing, transitions and about half of the scenes. In the new version, each idea gets two layers: an elegant line-art animation taken from your animatic, then the real app screen proving it.

## 1. Voiceover 10% faster
- Speed the VO up 1.1× while keeping the voice's pitch natural (no chipmunk effect). It goes from 3:15 to about 2:57.
- Re-time every word on the faster audio, so all animations still land exactly on the spoken words.
- The film goes from 3:21 to about 3:03, including the end card.

## 2. Faster, still luxurious
- **Shorter holds:** each idea stays on screen about 30–40% less time. A new visual change every 2–3 seconds instead of 4–6.
- **No dead moments:** right now some scenes fade to an empty background before the next one starts. Every scene will flow straight into the next.
- **Constant gentle camera movement:** slow drift, push-in and parallax on everything, so the frame never feels frozen.
- **Smoother motion:** soft, eased acceleration on moves rather than mechanical linear motion. Fast, but never jerky.

## 3. The reference video's animations
**Rebuilt, not pasted.** The clips in your MP4 are low resolution (1024×576) and have Arabic labels in almost every frame, so dropping them in would look soft and break the English-only rule. Instead I'll recreate those animations sharp at 1080p60, in English, in the same line-art style, and pair each one with the real screen:

| VO moment | Line-art animation (from your animatic) | Then the real screen |
|---|---|---|
| "We build communities" | Gold skyline drawing itself on the wave line | Night photo of the community |
| "This is the ZOOD app" | Phone outline sketches itself, "ZOOD" appears | The line phone turns into the realistic iPhone with the splash screen |
| "Explore every destination" | Project list with a radar pulse | Map, then 3D city |
| "Choose your unit" | Stacked floors, "Floor 12" lifts out of the stack | 3D Walkthrough |
| "Real time / compare" | Unit grid lights up as available/sold, COMPARE card slides in | Compare screen |
| "Walk through your environment" | Isometric room, the Modern/Classic toggle changes the furniture | Corridor walk-through |
| "Sign it digitally" | Contract sheet with a "Swipe to sign" slider | E-Signing screen with the signature drawing |
| "Every payment / every stage" | Payment ring 0%→40% with milestone dots | Profile and Construction (68%) |
| "We take care of the details" | Floor plan with snag pins ("Scratch – kitchen", "In progress") | Handover checklist |
| "Protected securely" | Title deed card, vault lock closing | Profile |
| "Your community" | Shared-services pie chart and a filling noticeboard | Community screen |
| "There is something more" | Three flowing lines rising into a curve | Yield Manager |

## 4. New animations (the added visual polish)
1. **Morph transitions:** the line drawing turns into the real UI (lines fade, then the screen fills in).
2. **Phone continuity:** one hero phone flies between scenes, rotating and swapping screens in motion, instead of separate phones fading in and out.
3. **Screen zoom-throughs:** the camera dives into a screen and comes out into the next scene.
4. **UI pop-outs:** cards and buttons lift off the screen in 3D depth with soft shadows.
5. **Light sweeps:** a rose-gold sheen across the phone glass and the logo at key beats.
6. **Masked text reveals:** words slide up from behind a line, Apple-style, mixed with the existing blur reveals.
7. **Number tickers:** prices, percentages and unit counts counting up.
8. **Brand-line wipes:** the kinked ZOOD line sweeps across the screen as the transition between chapters.
9. **Finale upgrade:** the screen wall moves in a slow 3D sweep, the blocks assemble with a stagger, then fold into the icon and the logo with a light burst.

## 5. Scenes I'll drop or shorten
- The separate "Discover / Own / Live / Invest" title cards get shorter (about 0.6 s) and become quick line-wipe transitions.
- "Not four applications" becomes one quick move: four icons merge into one.
- The long full-screen photo holds (perfect home, enjoy the moment) are cut to about half.

## Questions before I start
1. **"Remove the unwanted cuts":** I took this to mean the moments where a scene fades to an empty background and then the next one starts, which I'll remove (section 2). Did you mean something else, like specific scenes you didn't like, or the pauses in the voiceover? If it's specific scenes, tell me which ones.

xf=int(0.012*sr); out=[]; pos=0
for c0,c1 in cuts:
    i0,i1=int(c0*sr),int(c1*sr)
    seg=a[pos:i0].copy()
    out.append(seg); pos=i1

# join with short crossfades
res=out[0]
for seg in out[1:]:

    fade=np.linspace(0,1,n)
    res=np.concatenate([res[:-n], res[-n:]*(1-fade)+seg[:n]*fade, seg[n:]])
removed=sum(c1-c0 for c0,c1 in cuts)
print('cuts',len(cuts),'removed',round(removed,2),'new len',round(len(res)/sr,2))
o=wave.open('vo_tight.wav','wb'); o.setnchannels(1); o.setsampwidth(2); o.setframerate(sr); o.writeframes(np.clip(res,-32768,32767).astype(np.int16).tobytes()); o.close()

        if mx>speech*0.08: bad.append((t,toks[i+1],round(a0,2),round(a1,2),round(mx/speech,2)))
print('speech rms',round(speech),'suspicious cuts:',len(bad)); print(bad)
EOF

**Tool · Bash** — Cut pauses using energy-based silence detection

````
S=/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-video/794afff8-8449-55f8-a931-dabd13875fea/scratchpad; cd $S && python3 - <<'EOF'
import json,re,wave,numpy as np
w=[x for x in json.load(open('words_timed.json')) if x[0] not in('<sil>','<s>','</s>')]
toks=re.findall(r"[A-Za-z']+[.,?]?",open('script.txt').read().replace('Long-term','Long term'))
wf=wave.open('vo48.wav'); sr=wf.getframerate(); a=np.frombuffer(wf.readframes(wf.getnframes()),dtype=np.int16).astype(np.float32)
hop=int(0.01*sr); n=len(a)//hop
rms=np.sqrt(np.mean(a[:n*hop].reshape(n,hop)**2,axis=1))
speech=np.sqrt(np.mean(a[int(5*sr):int(15*sr)]**2))
sil=rms<speech*0.035
runs=[];i=0
while i<n:
    if sil[i]:
        j=i
        while j<n and sil[j]: j+=1
        runs.append((i*0.01,j*0.01)); i=j
    else: i+=1
starts=[x[1] for x in w]
cuts=[]
for r0,r1 in runs:
    if r1-r0<0.2: continue
    if r0<0.05: cuts.append((0,max(0,r1-0.1))); continue
    if r1>len(a)/sr-0.05: continue
    k=max([idx for idx,s in enumerate(starts) if s<r0],default=0)
    t=toks[k]; tgt=0.32 if t[-1] in '.?' else (0.18 if t.endswith(',') else 0.13)
    if (r1-r0)>tgt+0.04:
        m=0.06  # keep tail
        cuts.append((r0+m, r0+m+(r1-r0-tgt)))
xf=int(0.008*sr); out=[];pos=0
for c0,c1 in cuts:
    out.append(a[pos:int(c0*sr)]); pos=int(c1*sr)
out.append(a[pos:])
res=out[0]
for seg in out[1:]:
    m=min(xf,len(res),len(seg)); f=np.linspace(0,1,m)
    res=np.concatenate([res[:-m],res[-m:]*(1-f)+seg[:m]*f,seg[m:]])
print('runs',len(runs),'cuts',len(cuts),'removed',round(sum(b-a_ for a_,b in cuts),2),'len',round(len(res)/sr,2))
json.dump(cuts,open('cuts.json','w'))
o=wave.open('vo_tight.wav','wb'); o.setnchannels(1);o.setsampwidth(2);o.setframerate(sr);o.writeframes(np.clip(res,-32768,32767).astype(np.int16).tobytes());o.close()
EOF

// ---------- VO cue lookup (VO comes from vo.js) ----------
const _norm = (s) => s.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z' ]/g, ' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
const _VOW = (typeof VO !== 'undefined' ? VO : []).map(v => _norm(v[0]));
function _find(phrase, k = 1) {
  const p = _norm(phrase).split(' ');
  let c = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i + p.length <= _VOW.length; i++) {
    if (p.every((x, j) => _VOW[i + j] === x) && ++c === k) return i;
  }
  throw new Error(`VO phrase not found: "${phrase}" #${k}`);
}
// start time of a spoken phrase (kth occurrence) / end time of its last word
const at = (phrase, k = 1) => VO[_find(phrase, k)][1];
const after = (phrase, k = 1) => VO[_find(phrase, k) + _norm(phrase).split(' ').length - 1][2];

function swapWords(list, parent, mk, { useRise = false } = {}) {
  const els = list.map(([s]) => mk(s));

| Invest → finale | The phone pulls back to the centre and the wall of screens assembles around it |
| Wall → blocks → icon → logo | Unchanged; already continuous |

**Tool · Bash** — Add portal and layering helpers

````
cat >> lib.js <<'EOF'

// ---------- continuity helpers ----------
// A layer with an explicit stacking order (z): chapters 0, frame 20, finale 40, hero phone 50, portals 60, labels 90.
function zlayer(z, cls = '') { const e = layer(cls); e.style.zIndex = z; return e; }
// On-stage rect of a phone's screen when it sits flat (no rotation) centred at (x, y) with scale s.
function screenRect(p, x, y = 540, s = 1) {
  const w = p.sw * s, h = p.sh * s, R = p.pw * 0.17, f = Math.round(p.pw * 0.013), b = Math.round(p.pw * 0.03);
  return { l: x - w / 2, t: y - h / 2, w, h, r: (R - f - b) * s };
}
const insetFor = (r) => `inset(${r.t}px ${W - r.l - r.w}px ${H - r.t - r.h}px ${r.l}px round ${r.r}px)`;
const FULL = 'inset(0px 0px 0px 0px round 0px)';
// Full-frame layer grows out of a rect (e.g. the phone screen) / shrinks back into one.
function portalOpen(e, t, rect, dur = 0.9) {
  tl.set(e, { autoAlpha: 1 }, t);
  tl.fromTo(e, { clipPath: insetFor(rect) }, { clipPath: FULL, duration: dur, ease: 'power3.inOut', immediateRender: false }, t);
}
function portalClose(e, t, rect, dur = 0.9, from = FULL) {
  tl.fromTo(e, { clipPath: from }, { clipPath: insetFor(rect), duration: dur, ease: 'power3.inOut', immediateRender: false }, t);
  tl.to(e, { autoAlpha: 0, duration: 0.2, ease: 'none' }, t + dur - 0.2);
}
EOF

## Claude — 2026-10-05 12:43

The new version is ready and I've sent you a review copy. It runs 2:54 instead of 3:21. I checked frames at every scene change in the final render; I can't listen to audio, so please give the voiceover a listen.

The copy I sent is compressed to fit the 30 MB upload limit, so it will look a bit soft. The full-quality 1080p60 file is about 210 MB, so it needs the GitHub route we discussed. Tell me when you want it, but don't wait long: it only exists in this cloud session, which gets cleared after a period of inactivity.

**Voiceover:**
- I shortened the pauses between sentences and sped the voice up 10% without changing its pitch.
- Cuts were only made where the audio is actually silent, so no words are clipped.
- Every animation is still timed to the word it goes with.

**Continuity (instead of hard cuts):**
- **One phone throughout:** the same iPhone stays on screen from "This is the ZOOD app" to the end of Invest. It moves, turns and changes screens rather than being swapped for a new one.
- **Opening as one shot:** the "Luxury." period opens up into the copper texture. The copper shrinks into a photo card, which becomes the arch and then fills the screen with the reception photo. That photo fades into the "Traditionally" scene.
- **The animatic sequence:** the gold dot draws the skyline, the journey cards grow out of the skyline, and the line-drawn phone turns into the real iPhone.
- **Diving through the phone:**
  - The camera dives through the 3D room into the corridor, then the corridor shrinks back into the phone screen.
  - It dives through the phone into "perfect home", which shrinks back into the phone as it switches to Login.
  - For handover, the phone lays flat and becomes the floor plan.
  - The "Enjoy the moment" photo shrinks into the phone to start Live.
- **Ending:** the phone pulls back to the centre as the wall of screens builds around it. The wall turns into the grid of blocks, which folds into the app icon and then the logo.
- **Hard cuts left:** none of the scene changes is an instant switch any more. Background colour changes are slow fades behind the phone.

**From your reference animatic:** I rebuilt its animations sharp and in English, and kept every scene. That covers the skyline, the line-drawn phone, the radar rings, the stacked floors with "Floor 12", the room with the Modern/Classic toggle, the unit-availability grid, swipe-to-sign, the payment ring and milestones, the snag pins on the floor plan, the title deed with the vault lock, the services pie chart with the noticeboard, and the flowing lines.

The code is pushed to [MehfoozurRehman/video#1](https://github.com/MehfoozurRehman/video/pull/1). Background music is still not added.

// ---------- live footage (frame sequence of the ZOOD project film, 30 fps) ----------
// Shot list: [in, out] seconds in the project film.
const SHOT = {
  sunrise: [0.2, 6.0], haze: [6.6, 11.3], aerial: [11.6, 17.0], frontal: [17.3, 22.8], street: [23.1, 28.4], bench: [28.7, 31.0],
  boulevard: [31.2, 34.6], garden: [34.9, 40.3], arcade: [40.6, 46.1], window: [46.4, 51.6], pergola: [51.9, 57.4], kids: [57.7, 60.1],
  reflection: [60.3, 66.0], pool: [66.3, 71.9], interior: [72.1, 74.6], dusk: [74.9, 80.3], facade: [80.5, 83.1], dining: [83.4, 85.9],
  pavilion: [86.2, 90.7], swim: [90.9, 94.6], night: [94.9, 103.4],
};
const CLIPS = [];
const BLANK = 'data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==';
// Footage element filling its parent. Plays shot `name` from timeline t0 (until t1) at `rate`; holds the last frame.
function vclip(parent, name, t0, t1, { rate = 1, from = 0, pos = 'center', style = '' } = {}) {
  const [a, b] = SHOT[name];
  const img = el(`<img src="${BLANK}" style="position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;object-position:${pos};${style}">`, parent);
  CLIPS.push({ img, a: a + from, b, t0, t1, rate, last: -1 });
  return img;
}
// Called from __seek: point every active clip at the right frame and wait for decode.
function updateClips(t) {
  const jobs = [];
  for (const c of CLIPS) {
    if (t < c.t0 - 0.2 || t > c.t1 + 0.2) continue;
    const src = Math.min(c.b, Math.max(c.a, c.a + (t - c.t0) * c.rate));
    const n = Math.min(3131, Math.max(1, Math.round(src * 30) + 1));
    if (n !== c.last) {
      c.last = n;
      c.img.src = `assets/clips/proj/f${String(n).padStart(5, '0')}.jpg`;
      jobs.push(c.img.decode().catch(() => {}));
    }
  }
  return Promise.all(jobs);
}

// Ambient motion for plain backgrounds: drifting brand lines + two slow light glows.
function ambient(L, t0, t1, { color = 'rgba(214,165,140,.10)', glow = 'rgba(155,203,235,.10)', glow2 = 'rgba(214,165,140,.10)', seed = 2 } = {}) {
  const A = el('<div class="layer" style="overflow:hidden"></div>');

  const g1 = el(`<div class="abs" style="left:-300px;top:-200px;width:1100px;height:1100px;border-radius:50%;background:radial-gradient(circle, ${glow} 0%, rgba(0,0,0,0) 65%)"></div>`, A);
  const g2 = el(`<div class="abs" style="left:1100px;top:300px;width:1000px;height:1000px;border-radius:50%;background:radial-gradient(circle, ${glow2} 0%, rgba(0,0,0,0) 65%)"></div>`, A);
  const kl = kinkLines(A, { n: 18, color, width: 1.6, seed, dx: 46 });
  kl.svg.style.width = '2400px'; kl.svg.setAttribute('width', 2400);
  const d = t1 - t0;
  tl.fromTo(kl.svg, { x: 0 }, { x: -420, duration: d, ease: 'none', immediateRender: false }, t0);
  tl.fromTo(g1, { x: 0, y: 0 }, { x: 700, y: 260, duration: d, ease: 'sine.inOut', immediateRender: false }, t0);
  tl.fromTo(g2, { x: 0, y: 0 }, { x: -800, y: -380, duration: d, ease: 'sine.inOut', immediateRender: false }, t0);
  return A;
}
EOF

## Claude — 2026-10-05 13:56

Version 4 is ready and I've sent you a review copy (2:54, compressed to fit the 30 MB limit). I checked frames from across the full-quality render and they match what I designed. The voiceover is the same audio you already approved.

**Your project footage is now the main imagery:**
- **Opening:** "Luxury." over the sunrise aerial, opening into the facade close-up for "in every detail".
- **The "More ___" lines:** each one gets its own clip: the couple walking, the boulevard, the interior, the infinity pool and dusk dining.
- **Cream section:** pergola plaza, then three arches (reflection pool, rooftop pool, arcade), then the kids at the fountain for "happiness", then the couple on the bench full screen for "experience you live".
- **"We build communities":** the line drawing of the skyline sits over the real aerial, so the drawing turns into the actual project. The aerial carries on, blurred, behind the four journey cards, which each play their own clip.
- **Inside the app story:**
  - **Discover:** hazy aerial behind the phone, the interior for "walk through your environment", and the woman at the window for "perfect home".
  - **Own:** the street shot in the LIVE construction card.
  - **"Enjoy the moment":** the pool pavilion.
  - **Live:** the pergola plaza behind the community scene, and the night aerial behind the phone for "day and night".
  - **Invest:** the dusk towers.
- **Ending:** the night aerial behind the logo and the end card.

**More motion (including the 7–12 s and 12–26 s parts you mentioned):**
- **7–12 s:** the frame moves to a new layout on every word: card on the right, card on the left, full screen, centred arch, then a wide band. The text moves sides with it.
- **12–26 s:**
  - A set of floating objects drifts in, then scatters on "more things".
  - The arch splits into three, then joins back into one for "happiness".
  - A sheet of paper floats in and flips away on "promise on paper".

B uses the same voiceover, rules and brand kit as A, but a different visual language throughout. Here is how B's scenes look:

- **Opening:** "LUXURY" in giant letters with the sunrise footage playing inside them. The camera zooms through a letter, then four detail clips slice in as vertical panels for "in every detail".
- **"More ___":** a fast word ticker with "MORE" in outline type and a 01/05 counter. The footage behind is revealed through brand-stripe bands, a different clip for each word.
- **Magazine-style section:** a cream page with footage on one side, and the dividing line moves on every sentence.
  - "THINGS" stacks up and gets crossed out.
  - Frame corners close in on the walking couple for "designed around you".
  - "HAPPINESS" is filled with the kids-at-the-fountain clip.
  - A paper page turns away for "not a promise on paper".
- **"Traditionally":** forms, spreadsheets and messages are dealt across the screen like cards while a step counter races to 47. The big words slam in, then the pile stacks itself into the ZOOD app icon.
- **"We build communities":** five footage columns slide past. The four journey words fly across the screen. The columns become phone shapes and merge into one phone, with a giant "ZOOD" scrolling behind it.
- **Chapter openers:** each chapter opens with a full-screen colour block and a giant number (01–04).
- **Discover:** a flat phone with thin callout lines labelling Layouts, Views and Neighborhood, plus a magnifier lens on the 3D city.
  - Numbered steps 01–04, and the phone spins.
  - A live "95 units" counter with animated bars.
  - The phone splits into two for a "VS" comparison.
  - Filter switches flip on as each word is spoken.
  - "HOME" is filled with the window footage.
- **Own:** an identity ring counting to 100%, and a Request → Visit → Reserve progress line.
  - A giant signature written across the screen, then a "SIGNED" stamp.
  - Big counters, a tower of floors stacking up to 68%, and fanned-out monthly reports.
  - The LIVE footage split, and a handover checklist in big type.
  - "Enjoy the moment" seen through the ZOOD symbol, which then opens to full screen.
- **Live:** "YOUR HOME / YOUR PROPERTY" scrolling across in giant type, a vault dial, and a mosaic of six footage tiles. Then the ticker again, service tiles flipping in, a chat with a typing indicator, and a day/night slider sweeping across.
- **Invest:** "FOR THOSE WHO INVEST" over the dusk towers, a yield chart drawing itself, three option cards that reshuffle as each option is spoken, and a 00:03 timer.
- **Finale:** four footage panels for the four words, then bars that pulse with the narrator's voice. The bars fold into the ZOOD symbol, followed by a split end card: night aerial on the left, logo and store badges on the right.

The code is pushed to [MehfoozurRehman/video#1](https://github.com/MehfoozurRehman/video/pull/1). Background music is still not added to either video.

Here's a prompt that recreates this clip. It's a 3.3-second, 1280×720 shot of a 3D apartment furniture configurator inside the ZOOD app.

**Tip for an exact match:** use an image-to-video tool (Veo, Kling, Runway or Sora) and give it the first frame of this clip as the start image, plus the top-down floor plan (the last frame) as the end image if the tool supports end frames. Text alone won't reproduce the same apartment layout.

---

**Prompt**

> Photorealistic 3D architectural visualization of a luxury three-bedroom apartment, shown as a cut-away dollhouse model with the roof removed and walls cut at waist height, floating on a soft pale blue-grey studio background (#E8EEF3) with a gentle contact shadow. The interiors are bright, minimal and high-end: light oak floors, warm white walls, beige and soft-grey upholstery, sheer curtains, potted plants, a living room with an L-shaped sofa, a TV wall with slatted oak panels and a round coffee table, a dining area, three bedrooms with grey bedding, two bathrooms and a balcony. Soft natural daylight with subtle ambient occlusion, clean architectural-render quality, no people.
>
> **App interface overlay (flat, clean, iOS-style):**
> - Top-left: the ZOOD logo in navy (#041E42).
> - Under the logo: two white circular icon buttons, an analytics chart icon with a small red notification dot, and a shopping-cart icon.
> - Bottom centre: a white rounded pill with a sliders icon, a style label and a trash icon. Below it, a horizontal furniture carousel of white rounded cards with sofa and furniture thumbnails. One card is selected with a thin navy outline. The carousel has circular left and right arrow buttons and a thin progress bar underneath.
>
> **Action, in order:**
> 1. **0.0–0.3 s:** the camera holds a three-quarter isometric view from about 45° above. The style pill reads "Modern". A small floating "duplicate" tooltip icon sits above the hallway.
> 2. **0.3–1.0 s:** the pill switches to "Classic". The furniture in every room morphs into classic pieces in a quick shimmering, translucent white-glass dissolve: tufted sofas with carved legs, ornate armchairs and a classic dining set. The carousel slides left to show the classic sofa and armchair sets, with the selection outline moving to a classic sofa.
> 3. **1.0–1.9 s:** a slow, smooth orbit. The camera rotates around the model about 20–25° clockwise while staying at the same height. The furniture is now settled and the carousel stays visible.
> 4. **1.9–2.3 s:** the camera rises and rotates into a straight-down, top-down view. As it does, the pill, the carousel and the two icon buttons fade out. Only the logo remains.
> 5. **2.3–3.3 s:** the camera holds a clean top-down floor-plan view of the whole apartment, slightly zoomed in. Accent furniture pops in one at a time with a small bounce, each settling with a soft shadow: dusty-blue armchairs in the living room and hallway, a white swivel accent chair and a blue side chair in the bedroom.
>
> **Style:** smooth, eased camera motion with no hard cuts. Premium real-estate product demo, crisp detail, soft shadows, a bright airy colour palette. Camera: virtual 35 mm lens, gentle ease-in/ease-out on every move. 16:9, 30 fps, about 3.5 seconds.
>
> **Negative prompt:** people, text errors, warped furniture, flickering, dark lighting, fisheye, clutter, watermark, blurry UI.

---

**If you're giving this to a 3D artist instead of an AI tool, the shot list in brief:**
1. A 0.3 s hold on the isometric dollhouse ("Modern").
2. A 0.7 s furniture-style swap to "Classic", with a glassy dissolve and the carousel scrolling.
3. A 0.9 s clockwise orbit of about 25°.
4. A 0.4 s crane up to top-down while the UI fades out.
5. A 1.0 s top-down hold while accent chairs pop in one at a time.

Separately, the corrected full-quality Video B (with the caption overlap fixed) is still rendering in the background.

**Tool · Bash** — Detect hard cuts with frame differencing

````
S=/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-video/794afff8-8449-55f8-a931-dabd13875fea/scratchpad; D="$S/f4/New folder (4)"; cat > $S/cuts4.py <<'E'
import sys,subprocess,numpy as np
f=sys.argv[1]; w,h=64,36
raw=subprocess.run(['ffmpeg','-v','error','-i',f,'-vf',f'scale={w}:{h}','-f','rawvideo','-pix_fmt','gray','-'],capture_output=True).stdout
a=np.frombuffer(raw,np.uint8).reshape(-1,h,w).astype(float)
d=np.abs(np.diff(a,axis=0)).mean(axis=(1,2))
med=np.median(d)
print(' '.join(f'{(i+1)/24:.2f}s({v:.0f})' for i,v in enumerate(d) if v>max(12,4*med)))
E
for i in $(seq 1 17); do echo -n "P$i: "; python3 -I $S/cuts4.py "$D/P$i.mp4"; done
````

**Tool · Write** — /home/user/video/tools/prep_clips.py

````
"""Turn the generated / client clips into frame sequences the film can seek frame-accurately.

  python3 -I tools/prep_clips.py <clips.json> <out_dir>

clips.json: [{"name", "src", "mode": "plain"|"key"|"screen", "t0", "t1", "crop": [x, y, w, h], "spill": 1}]
  plain   JPEG frames at the source resolution and frame rate (no scaling, no frame-rate change)
  key     green removed -> WebP with alpha
  screen  like key, plus the 4 corners of the green screen per frame (for mapping app UI onto it)
Writes <out_dir>/<name>/fNNNN.(jpg|webp) and <out_dir>/clips.js (frame counts, fps, size, screen quads).
"""
import json, os, subprocess, sys
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage

cfg = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
OUT = sys.argv[2]
meta = {}


def probe(src):
    r = subprocess.run(['ffprobe', '-v', 'error', '-select_streams', 'v:0', '-show_entries', 'stream=width,height,r_frame_rate',
                        '-of', 'csv=p=0', src], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip().split(',')
    a, b = r[2].split('/')
    return int(r[0]), int(r[1]), float(a) / float(b)


def frames(src, w, h):
    p = subprocess.Popen(['ffmpeg', '-v', 'error', '-i', src, '-f', 'rawvideo', '-pix_fmt', 'rgb24', '-'], stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
    n = w * h * 3
    while True:
        b = p.stdout.read(n)
        if len(b) < n:
            break
        yield np.frombuffer(b, np.uint8).reshape(h, w, 3)


def key(a, t0, t1, spill):
    f = a.astype(np.float32)
    r, g, b = f[..., 0], f[..., 1], f[..., 2]
    d = g - np.maximum(r, b)
    alpha = np.clip((t1 - d) / (t1 - t0), 0, 1)
    # despill: pull green down to the level of the other channels near the key
    near = ndimage.maximum_filter((alpha < 0.98).astype(np.uint8), size=9) > 0 if spill == 1 else np.ones_like(alpha, bool)
    lim = np.maximum(r, b) + 4
    g2 = np.where(near & (g > lim), lim, g)
    rgb = np.stack([r, g2, b], -1)
    return np.dstack([rgb, alpha * 255]).clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8), alpha


def quad(alpha, min_area):
    m = alpha < 0.5
    m = ndimage.binary_closing(m, iterations=6)
    lab, n = ndimage.label(m)
    if n == 0:
        return None
    sizes = ndimage.sum(m, lab, range(1, n + 1))
    k = int(np.argmax(sizes)) + 1
    if sizes[k - 1] < min_area:
        return None
    ys, xs = np.nonzero(lab == k)
    s, t = xs + ys, xs - ys
    pts = [(xs[s.argmin()], ys[s.argmin()]), (xs[t.argmax()], ys[t.argmax()]), (xs[s.argmax()], ys[s.argmax()]), (xs[t.argmin()], ys[t.argmin()])]

// Video A (v5) additions, loaded after lib.js. Video B never loads this file.
// - the new ZOOD brand line (thin vertical stroke whose kink swells into a tapered S)
// - generated / client clips as frame sequences (assets/clips/gen, see tools/prep_clips.py)
// - app UI mapped onto green phone / tablet screens, frame by frame

// ---------- brand line ----------
// One line: x at the top, kinks at y=k over height kh, ends at x+dx. Thin half-width a, swells to b.
function brandLineD(x, k, dx, { h = H, a = 1.4, b = 7, kh = 150, top = -20 } = {}) {
  const N = 28, L = [], R = [];
  const y0 = k - kh / 2;
  const ss = (u) => u * u * (3 - 2 * u);
  L.push([x - a, top]); R.push([x + a, top]);
  for (let i = 0; i <= N; i++) {
    const u = i / N, y = y0 + kh * u;
    const cx = x + dx * ss(u);
    // swell is strongest just after the middle of the S, like the brand drawing
    const sw = a + (b - a) * Math.pow(Math.sin(Math.PI * Math.min(1, u * 1.05)), 2.2);
    const slope = 6 * u * (1 - u) * dx / kh;               // dx/dy of the centre line
    const off = sw * Math.sqrt(1 + slope * slope);         // keep the stroke width perpendicular
    L.push([cx - off, y]); R.push([cx + off, y]);
  }
  L.push([x + dx - a, h + 20]); R.push([x + dx + a, h + 20]);

  const paths = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const x = x0 + (x1 - x0) * (i + 0.2 + r() * 0.6) / n;
    const k = h * (0.2 + 0.6 * r()), d = (r() > 0.5 ? 1 : -1) * dx * (0.8 + r() * 0.5);
    const add = (xx, kk) => {
      const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path');
      p.setAttribute('d', brandLineD(xx, kk, d, { h, a, b, kh })); p.setAttribute('fill', color);
      svg.appendChild(p); paths.push(p);
    };
    add(x, k);
    if (r() < 0.3) add(x + 16, k + 12);                    // a close twin, as in the "Simple" artwork
  }
  return { svg, paths };
}

# ZOOD — App Launch Film

A 2:54 landscape (1920×1080, 60fps) launch film for the ZOOD mobile app, built as code:
an HTML/CSS stage animated by a single paused GSAP timeline, rendered frame-by-frame with
headless Chromium (Playwright) and encoded with ffmpeg.

## Two films
- **Video A** — `src/index.html` + `src/scenes.js` (floating 3D phone, travelling frame, portals).
- **Video B** — `src/b.html` + `src/scenes-b.js` (editorial rhythm: footage inside type and the ZOOD symbol, stripe wipes, split screens, sliding footage columns, marquee type, flat phones with UI annotations). Render with `FILM=b.html node render/render.mjs --out out/ZOOD_B.mp4`.

Both share `src/lib.js`, `src/boot.js`, `src/style.css`, `src/vo.js` and the renderer.

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `src/index.html` | The 1920×1080 stage |
| `src/style.css` | Brand tokens (Navy #041E42, Beige #DBC8B6, Rose Gold #A27063, Sky #9BCBEB), type scale, phone mockup |
| `src/lib.js` | Helpers: text reveals, iPhone mockup, screen push, tap ripples, counters, brand curve lines |
| `src/scenes.js` | The whole timeline, scene by scene. Times are seconds into the VO |
| `src/boot.js` | Grain/vignette, asset preloading, `__seek(t)` API, `?play` live preview |
| `render/render.mjs` | Parallel frame renderer → MP4 with VO |
| `render/still.mjs` | Render stills at given times for review |

            lab, _ = ndimage.label(ndimage.binary_opening(w > 0.5, iterations=2))
            edge = set(np.unique(np.concatenate([lab[0], lab[-1], lab[:, 0], lab[:, -1]]))) - {0}
            bgm = ndimage.gaussian_filter(ndimage.binary_dilation(np.isin(lab, list(edge)), iterations=4).astype(np.float32), 3)

            Image.fromarray(out.clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(f'{d}/f{n:04d}.jpg', quality=95, subsampling=0)
            continue"""

- The star emblem (the new P16) spins in a tile in the final grid.

**Tool · Bash** — Add live-screen support to lib-a and boot

````
cat >> lib-a.js <<'EOF'

// ---------- live app screens (the 31 ZOOD screens, 390×844 HTML pages in assets/ui) ----------
// A screen source is either an image path or 'ui:NN'. Live screens are iframes scaled into the phone,
// so text stays sharp and their parts can be animated on the film timeline once loaded (onUI).
window.READY_WAIT = window.READY_WAIT || [];
window.UI_ANIM = window.UI_ANIM || [];
const UIW = 390, UIH = 844;
function scrContent(src, sw, sh) {
  if (!src.startsWith('ui:')) return el(`<div class="scrw"><img src="${src}"></div>`);
  const id = src.slice(3);
  const s = Math.max(sw / UIW, sh / UIH);
  const w = el(`<div class="scrw" style="background:#F4EEE8"></div>`);
  const f = el(`<iframe src="assets/ui/${id}.html" scrolling="no" style="position:absolute;left:${(sw - UIW * s) / 2}px;top:${(sh - UIH * s) / 2}px;width:${UIW}px;height:${UIH}px;border:0;transform:scale(${s});transform-origin:0 0;pointer-events:none"></iframe>`, w);
  window.READY_WAIT.push(new Promise(res => f.addEventListener('load', async () => {
    try { await f.contentDocument.fonts.ready; await Promise.all([...f.contentDocument.images].map(i => i.decode().catch(() => {}))); } catch (e) {}
    res();
  }, { once: true })));
  w.ifr = f;
  return w;
}
// Run fn(doc, q) after the screen's page has loaded: q(sel) → first match, q.all(sel) → all matches.
function onUI(w, fn) {
  window.UI_ANIM.push(() => {
    const d = w.ifr.contentDocument;
    const q = (s) => d.querySelector(s); q.all = (s) => [...d.querySelectorAll(s)];
    fn(d, q);
  });
}
// Element whose own text matches exactly (for counting up numbers inside a screen).
function uiText(d, txt) {
  return [...d.querySelectorAll('body *')].find(e => [...e.childNodes].some(n => n.nodeType === 3 && n.textContent.trim() === txt));
}
function uiCount(d, txt, t, dur = 1.2, from = 0) {
  const e = uiText(d, txt); if (!e) throw new Error('ui text not found: ' + txt);
  const n = [...e.childNodes].find(c => c.nodeType === 3 && c.textContent.trim() === txt);
  const target = parseFloat(txt.replace(/[^0-9.]/g, '')), dec = (txt.split('.')[1] || '').replace(/[^0-9]/g, '').length;
  const fmt = (v) => txt.replace(/[0-9][0-9,]*(\.[0-9]+)?/, dec ? v.toFixed(dec) : Math.round(v).toLocaleString('en-US'));
  const o = { v: from };
  tl.fromTo(o, { v: from }, { v: target, duration: dur, ease: 'power2.out', immediateRender: true, onUpdate: () => { n.textContent = fmt(o.v); } }, t);
}
// Staggered rise-in of items inside a screen.

// Text that changes at given times: pairs [[t, text], ...] (deterministic under seeking).

  const node = [...e.childNodes].find(c => c.nodeType === 3 && c.textContent.trim()) || e.firstChild;

}

## Claude — 2026-10-07 08:03

Now building the automatic overlap check: it scans the whole film and flags any frame where visible text overlaps a phone, window or card.


**Tool · Write** — /home/user/video/tools/check_overlap.mjs

````
// Scans the film for on-screen text that overlaps a phone, a framed window or a card it does not belong to.
// node tools/check_overlap.mjs [step=0.2] [start=0] [end=DURATION]
import { openFilm } from '../render/page.mjs';
const [step = 0.2, start = 0, endArg] = process.argv.slice(2).map(Number);
const f = await openFilm();
const end = endArg || f.duration;
const hits = [];
for (let t = start; t <= end; t += step) {
  await f.page.evaluate((t) => window.__seek(t), t);
  const r = await f.page.evaluate(() => {
    const vis = (e) => {
      let o = 1;
      for (let n = e; n && n.nodeType === 1; n = n.parentElement) {
        const cs = getComputedStyle(n);
        if (cs.display === 'none' || cs.visibility === 'hidden') return 0;
        o *= parseFloat(cs.opacity);
        if (o < 0.35) return o;
      }
      return o;
    };
    const box = (e) => e.getBoundingClientRect();
    const inView = (b) => b.width > 2 && b.height > 2 && b.right > 0 && b.bottom > 0 && b.left < 1920 && b.top < 1080;
    const obs = [...document.querySelectorAll('.phone, [data-ob], .tile, .card, .chip')].filter(e => inView(box(e)) && vis(e) > 0.5);
    const words = [...document.querySelectorAll('.w')].filter(e => e.textContent.trim() && inView(box(e)) && vis(e) > 0.5);
    const out = [];
    for (const w of words) {
      const a = box(w);
      for (const o of obs) {
        if (o.contains(w)) continue;
        const b = box(o);
        const ox = Math.min(a.right, b.right) - Math.max(a.left, b.left), oy = Math.min(a.bottom, b.bottom) - Math.max(a.top, b.top);
        if (ox > 6 && oy > 6) out.push(`"${w.textContent.trim()}" × ${o.className || o.dataset.ob} (${Math.round(ox)}×${Math.round(oy)})`);
      }
    }
    return [...new Set(out)];
  });
  if (r.length) hits.push(`${t.toFixed(1)}s  ${r.slice(0, 4).join(' | ')}`);
}
console.log(hits.length ? hits.join('\n') : 'no overlaps');
await f.browser.close();
````

segs=[('everything you need','as if zood'),('as if zood','day and night'),('day and night','and for those who'),('and for those who','long term'),('your home','and everything your'),('more presence','everything you need')]

"""Edit a voiceover take for the film and force-align it to the script.

  python3 -I tools/vo_edit.py <take.mp3|wav> <script.txt> <out.wav> <out_vo.js> [tempo=1.1]

1. align the raw take to the script (pocketsphinx)
2. tighten pauses: 0.30 s after . ?, 0.17 s after a comma, 0.12 s between words (12 ms crossfades)
3. speed up with atempo (pitch kept)
4. align the edited take again and write the word timings as `const VO = [[word, start, end], ...]`
"""

words = [re.sub(r'[^a-z\']', '', t.lower()) for t in toks]
tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()


def pcm(f, sr):
    o = os.path.join(tmp, f'a{sr}.wav')
    subprocess.run(['ffmpeg', '-v', 'error', '-y', '-i', f, '-ar', str(sr), '-ac', '1', '-c:a', 'pcm_s16le', o], check=True)
    w = wave.open(o)
    return np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()), np.int16), o

    a, _ = pcm(f, 16000)
    d = Decoder(samprate=16000, bestpath=False, loglevel='ERROR')
    d.add_word('zood', 'Z UW D', True)
    for w in sorted(set(words)):
        if d.lookup_word(w) is None:
            sys.exit(f'not in dictionary: {w}')
    d.set_align_text(' '.join(words))

    d.set_alignment()
    d.start_utt(); d.process_raw(raw, full_utt=True); d.end_utt()
    r = [(s.name, s.start / 100, (s.start + s.duration) / 100) for s in d.get_alignment() if s.name not in ('<sil>', '<s>', '</s>')]
    if [x[0] for x in r] != words:
        sys.exit('alignment does not follow the script')
    return r

import sys,subprocess,re,difflib
from pocketsphinx import Decoder
raw=subprocess.run(['ffmpeg','-v','error','-i',sys.argv[1],'-ar','16000','-ac','1','-f','s16le','-'],capture_output=True).stdout
d=Decoder(samprate=16000,loglevel='ERROR')
hyp=[]
step=16000*2*20
for i in range(0,len(raw),step):
    d.start_utt(); d.process_raw(raw[i:i+step],full_utt=True); d.end_utt()
    if d.hyp(): hyp+=d.hyp().hypstr.split()
ref=re.sub(r"[^a-z' ]"," ",open(sys.argv[2]).read().lower()).split()
sm=difflib.SequenceMatcher(None,ref,hyp,autojunk=False)
print('ratio',round(sm.ratio(),3),len(ref),len(hyp))
E
for f in $S/vo7/vo-edit.wav $S/v6bak/vo-edit.wav; do python3 -I $S/asr.py $f $S/script.txt; done

}

}

**Tool · Bash** — Measure VO level evenness in 3 s windows

````
python3 -I - <<'E'
import subprocess,numpy as np
r=subprocess.run(['ffmpeg','-v','error','-i','src/assets/audio/vo-edit.wav','-ac','1','-ar','16000','-f','f32le','-'],capture_output=True).stdout
a=np.frombuffer(r,np.float32); w=16000*3
lv=[(i/16000,20*np.log10(np.sqrt(np.mean(a[i:i+w]**2))+1e-9)) for i in range(0,len(a)-w,w)]
sp=[(t,l) for t,l in lv if l>-40]
m=np.median([l for t,l in sp])
print('median',round(m,1)); print('3s windows deviating >3 dB:',[(round(t),round(l-m,1)) for t,l in sp if abs(l-m)>3])
print('around day and night:',[(round(t),round(l-m,1)) for t,l in lv if 128<t<146])
E

## Claude — 2026-10-08 09:00

The final English film is finished: 2:53, with the 720p review copy sent above (28 MB). The pause after "…not just an empty room." is now 3 seconds, as you asked.

**Files** (in `out/`):
- `ZOOD_App_Film_v7_1080p60.mp4`: the master with voice and music, at −16.2 LUFS (same loudness as v6).
- `ZOOD_App_Film_v7_voice_1080p60.mp4`: the same picture with voice only.
- `ZOOD_v7_review.mp4`: the 720p review copy.

**What I checked:**
- **Picture and sound:** I watched the whole master at two frames per second and also used automatic checks. There are no black or frozen frames. The voice level is even all the way through, including "always with you… day and night".
- **Text:** no caption sits behind or over any image or phone at any point. Every caption matches the voiceover word for word, and ZOOD is always in capitals.
- **Furniture:** the client's points are covered. The three packages show with their prices, only one is selected at a time, the details show the cost of each piece, and no furniture appears during "Verify your identity".

**Fixed during my watch-throughs:**
- The opening "More…" lines no longer cross the moving image frames.
- Two captions that were shortened versions of the voiceover now match it exactly.
- Each word in the "Traditionally…" list and the final Discover / Enjoy / Live / Dwell now leaves before the next one appears.
- The "That is why, at ZOOD…" lines now appear in the right order.
- I removed a short empty navy gap before construction tracking.
- "Perfect home" uses a deeper rose so it reads on the light background.
- The 3D room model now sits to the right of the captions, with no visible edge around it.

**GitHub:** everything is pushed to `claude/intelligent-allen-jrzv18`. I force-pushed to replace only the malicious commit, so the branch is now clean. The `main` branch still has its own copy of that malicious commit (`544e749`). I haven't touched `main`; clean it once the affected machine has been cleaned. The video files and client assets stay out of the repository because it's public.

The Arabic version can be built on this same setup whenever you're ready.

**Tool · Bash** — Write and apply a button repair tool, re-screenshot

````
S=/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-video/794afff8-8449-55f8-a931-dabd13875fea/scratchpad; mkdir -p $S/ui_orig && cp -n src/assets/ui/[0-9][0-9].html $S/ui_orig/ 2>/dev/null; cp $S/build7/09.orig.html $S/ui_orig/09.html; cat > tools/fix_ui_buttons.py <<'E'
"""Repair buttons whose styles the design export expanded into hundreds of `unset` properties.

  python3 -I tools/fix_ui_buttons.py src/assets/ui/NN.html ...

The expansion keeps colours but loses the button's padding and corner radius, so pills turn into
hard rectangles squeezed around their label. Each such button gets its radius back (half its height,
a pill like the app's other buttons) and, when it has no fixed width, side padding.
"""
import re, sys

def fix(style):
    if 'padding: unset' not in style:
        return style
    get = lambda k: (re.search(rf'(?<![-\w]){k}: (?!unset)([^;]+)', style) or [None, None])[1]
    bg, bd = get('background') or get('background-color'), get('border-top') or get('border')
    if not bg and not bd:
        return style
    h = get('height')
    hv = float(re.match(r'[\d.]+', h).group()) if h and re.match(r'[\d.]+px', h) else 44.0
    add = []
    if not get('border-radius') or get('border-radius') in ('0px', '0'):
        add.append(f'border-radius:{hv / 2:g}px')
    if not get('width'):
        add.append(f'padding:0 {14 if hv <= 30 else 20}px')
    return style + ';' + ';'.join(add) if add else style

for p in sys.argv[1:]:
    s = open(p).read()
    n = [0]
    def rep(m):
        new = fix(m.group(2))
        n[0] += new != m.group(2)
        return m.group(1) + new + '"'
    s = re.sub(r'(<button[^>]*?style=")([^"]{3000,})"', rep, s)
    open(p, 'w').write(s)
    print(p, n[0], 'buttons repaired')
E

**Tool · Write** — /home/user/video/tools/fix_ui_buttons.py

````
"""Repair elements whose styles the design export expanded into hundreds of `unset` properties.

  python3 -I tools/fix_ui_buttons.py src/assets/ui/NN.html ...

The expansion keeps the element's real `padding` and `border-radius`, but later in the same style it
also writes the logical longhands (`padding-inline-start: unset`, `border-start-start-radius: unset`, ...),
which reset them. Pills turn into hard rectangles squeezed around their label. The real values are
re-asserted at the end of the style so they win again.
"""
import re, sys

PROPS = ('padding', 'border-radius', 'margin', 'border', 'border-top', 'border-right', 'border-bottom', 'border-left')


def fix(style):
    keep = [f'{k}:{v}' for k, v in re.findall(r'(?:^|;)\s*([\w-]+):\s*([^;]+)', style) if k in PROPS and v.strip() != 'unset']
    return style.rstrip('; ') + ';' + ';'.join(keep) if keep else style


for p in sys.argv[1:]:
    s, n = open(p).read(), 0
    def rep(m):
        global n
        n += 1
        return m.group(1) + fix(m.group(2)) + '"'
    s = re.sub(r'(<[a-z]+[^>]*?style=")([^"]{3000,})"', rep, s)
    open(p, 'w').write(s)
    print(p, n, 'elements re-asserted')
````

// Stills of the live app screens at 2x (used where many screens tile, e.g. the finale wall).
// node tools/ui_png.mjs [NN ...]   (default: every src/assets/ui/NN.html)
import fs from 'fs';
import { chromium } from 'playwright-core';
const dir = new URL('../src/assets/ui/', import.meta.url).pathname;
const ids = process.argv.slice(2).length ? process.argv.slice(2) : fs.readdirSync(dir).filter(f => /^\d\d\.html$/.test(f)).map(f => f.slice(0, 2));
const b = await chromium.launch({ executablePath: process.env.CHROME || '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1194/chrome-linux/headless_shell', args: ['--allow-file-access-from-files'] });
const p = await b.newPage({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 }, deviceScaleFactor: 2 });
fs.mkdirSync(dir + 'png', { recursive: true });
for (const id of ids) {
  await p.goto(`file://${dir}${id}.html`);
  await p.evaluate(async () => { await document.fonts.ready; await Promise.all([...document.images].map(i => i.decode().catch(() => {}))); });
  await p.screenshot({ path: `${dir}png/${id}.png` });
}
console.log(ids.length, 'screens');
await b.close();
E

**Tool · Bash** — List all caption strings in scenes.js

````
python3 -I - <<'E'
import re
s=open('src/scenes.js').read()
caps=[]
for m in re.finditer(r"\b(ltext|ctext|text|chapterTitle|chip)\(\s*(['`])((?:\\.|(?!\2).)*)\2",s):
    caps.append((m.group(1),m.group(3)))
for m in re.finditer(r"swapWords\(\[(.*?)\]\s*,",s,re.S):
    for w in re.findall(r"\[\s*'([^']*)'",m.group(1)): caps.append(('swap',w))
seen=set()
for k,c in caps:
    if c in seen: continue
    seen.add(c); print(k,'|',c[:150])
print(len(seen))
E
````

"""Edit the Arabic voiceover and move every film cue onto it.

  python3 -I tools/vo_ar.py <take.mp3> <anchors.json> <english_vo.js> <out.wav> <out_vo.js> [target_seconds]

There is no Arabic speech model here, so the take is split at its pauses (silence detection) and
anchors.json pairs English script phrases with those speech segments:
  {"holds": {"<seg>": seconds, ...},
   "anchors": [["english phrase", k, "s12"], ["english phrase", k, "e12"], ["phrase", k, "s19+0.45"], ...]}
  "s12" = start of segment 12, "e12" = its end, "+0.45" = an offset into it (seconds of the raw take).

1. pauses are tightened (sentence ≥0.8 s → 0.42 s, phrase 0.4–0.8 s → 0.26 s, shorter kept up to 0.22 s),
   held beats are inserted after the named segments, 12 ms crossfades
2. tempo (pitch kept) brings the edit to target_seconds, never faster than 1.1×
3. every English word time is mapped onto the edited Arabic take through the anchors (linear in between),
   so the film's at('english phrase') cues land on the matching Arabic phrase. Written in vo.js format.

if len(v) % 2 == 1:  # take ends in speech

Adding the right-to-left styles. Letter-spacing has to be off for Arabic, because it breaks the letter joins. Also adding a pass that translates labels inside the film's own UI panels.


**Tool · Bash** — Add Arabic styles, UI translation pass, and list untranslated text

````
cat >> src/style.css <<'E'

/* ---------- Arabic film ---------- */
.ar { direction: rtl; letter-spacing: 0 !important; }
.lang-ar .label, .lang-ar .ar * { letter-spacing: 0 !important; }
.lang-ar .ar-ui { direction: rtl; letter-spacing: 0 !important; }
.lang-ar .app { font-family: Figtree, Huwiya, sans-serif; }
E
cat >> src/lib.js <<'E'

// Arabic film: labels inside the film's own UI (chapter labels, chips, cards, the packages screens) are
// translated in place after the scenes are built. Phone screens are the client's designs and stay English.
function arabizeStage() {
  if (!IS_AR) return [];
  stage.classList.add('lang-ar');
  const missing = new Set();
  const skip = (n) => n.closest('.ph-screen, iframe, .ar, svg');
  const walker = document.createTreeWalker(stage, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT);
  const nodes = [];
  for (let n = walker.nextNode(); n; n = walker.nextNode()) nodes.push(n);
  for (const n of nodes) {
    const p = n.parentElement, t = n.textContent.trim();
    if (!p || skip(p) || !/[A-Za-z]{2}/.test(t)) continue;
    const ar = AR_CHAPTER[t] ?? AR_UI[t] ?? AR[t];
    if (ar == null) { missing.add(t); continue; }
    n.textContent = n.textContent.replace(t, ar);
    p.classList.add('ar-ui');
  }
  return [...missing];
}

# ZOOD — App Launch Film

A 2:54 landscape (1920×1080, 60fps) launch film for the ZOOD mobile app, built as code:
an HTML/CSS stage animated by a single paused GSAP timeline, rendered frame-by-frame with
headless Chromium (Playwright) and encoded with ffmpeg.

## Two films
- **Video A** (v5) — `src/index.html` + `src/scenes.js` + `src/lib-a.js` (floating 3D phone, travelling frame, portals, the new tapered brand line, generated clips with app UI mapped onto green phone/tablet screens).
- **Video B** — `src/b.html` + `src/scenes-b.js` (editorial rhythm: footage inside type and the ZOOD symbol, stripe wipes, split screens, sliding footage columns, marquee type, flat phones with UI annotations). Render with

# ZOOD Video A: hand the project over to the user's own computer

## Context
The user wants to continue this project on their own computer instead of in this cloud session. The repository must contain everything I know about the project, so that a clone on their machine can render and keep editing straight away. They chose to push all assets into the repo, even though the repo is public.

## 1. Assets into git (`src/assets/`, 1.5 GB, 6,739 files, none over 45 MB)
- Remove `src/assets/` from `.gitignore`. Keep `node_modules/`, `out/` and ffmpeg logs ignored.
- Commit and push in batches, so no single push is too large:
  1. fonts, brand, photos, screens, pkg, ui
  2. audio
  3. clips/gen, one push per few clips
  4. clips/proj
- Push with retries after each batch.
- Also commit the clip source configs and the English VO script from the scratchpad into `tools/`, so voice and clip processing can be redone locally.
  - Configs: the clips JSONs used with `prep_clips.py` (`cfg*.json`, `scr.json`, `new.json`, `g2.json`).
  - Script: `script.txt` saved as `tools/vo-script-en.txt`.

**`HANDOFF.md`**, the project brain:
- **What the films are and their current state:**

  - review and delivery encodes
  - overlap check
  - caption check
  - VO re-edit (`vo_edit.py` / `vo_ar.py` with the held beats)
  - the UI button fix
  - UI PNG stills
- **How the code works:**
  - the timeline and `at()` cues
  - the `lib-a` helpers
  - live UI iframes and `onUI`

  - the anchors file for the Arabic timing

  - Render only when asked.
  - Captions word for word with the voice; ZOOD always in capitals.
  - No text behind images or phones.
  - Women in hijab; no green screen.
  - Video A only.
  - Use original components.
  - 1080p masters; review copies under 30 MB.
  - Ask for proper materials rather than

"""List the speech segments of a voiceover take (split at pauses), for pairing with tools/ar_anchors.json.

  python3 -I tools/ar_segments.py src/assets/audio/vo-ar-take.mp3

Uses the same silence detection as tools/vo_ar.py (-40 dB, 0.2 s), so segment numbers match its s12 / e12 references.
"""
import re, subprocess, sys
det = subprocess.run(['ffmpeg', '-hide_banner', '-i', sys.argv[1], '-af', 'silencedetect=n=-40dB:d=0.2', '-f', 'null', '-'],
                     capture_output=True, text=True).stderr
v = [float(x) for x in re.findall(r'silence_(?:start|end): ([0-9.]+)', det)]
segs = [(v[i], v[i + 1]) for i in range(1, len(v) - 1, 2)]
for k, (a, b) in enumerate(segs):
    gap = segs[k + 1][0] - b if k + 1 < len(segs) else 0
    print(f'{k:3d}  {a:7.2f}-{b:7.2f}  ({b - a:4.2f}s)  pause after {gap:4.2f}s')
E

A 2:54 landscape (1920×1080, 60fps) launch film for the ZOOD mobile app, built as code:
an HTML/CSS stage animated by a single paused GSAP timeline, rendered frame-by-frame with
headless Chromium (Playwright) and encoded with ffmpeg.

## Two films
- **Video A** (v8) — `src/index.html` (English), `src/index-ar.html` (Arabic), `src/index-enar.html` (English on the Arabic voice) + `src/scenes.js` + `src/lib-a.js` (floating 3D phone, travelling frame, portals, the new tapered brand line, generated clips with app UI mapped onto green phone/tablet screens).
- **Video B** — `src/b.html` + `src/scenes-b.js` (editorial rhythm: footage inside type and the ZOOD symbol, stripe wipes, split screens, sliding footage columns, marquee type, flat phones with UI annotations). Render with `FILM=b.html node render/render.mjs --out out/ZOOD_B.mp4`.

29:## Assets
35:npx playwright install chromium
